_comment: Cross-language contract for the tether#153 sign-in redirect.
PRODUCER: signInURL() in internal/auth/oauth/handlers.go, asserted end to end (handler + html/template) by internal/auth/oauth/signin_prompt_test.go.
CONSUMER: safeRedirectTarget() in web/src/AuthPage.tsx, asserted by web/src/oauthSignInRedirect.test.ts.

Both sides READ this file; neither generates it. A producer change turns the Go test red until wantAuthURL is updated here, and the updated string is then re-validated against the real consumer. That is the whole point: two hand-copied lists would each hold a different subset and both look complete.
rawQuery is assigned to r.URL.RawQuery verbatim, so it is the exact byte string the handler sees.

entries.label: typical-mcp-client-request
entries.why: The shape an MCP client actually sends. Every parameter here has to survive the round trip or the consent page comes back unusable.

entries.label: state-carrying-a-space-and-a-hash
entries.why: A '#' in a value must stay in the query and not become a fragment; '+' must still decode to a space after two encode/decode hops.

entries.label: percent-and-plus-in-a-value
entries.why: Percent-encoding survives being percent-encoded again by url.QueryEscape and decoded once by URLSearchParams.

entries.label: dot-dot-segments-percent-encoded-in-redirect-uri
entries.why: tether#117 A3 class 1: '..' segments collapse during URL parsing. Here they sit in a parameter VALUE, where they must not reach the path of the assembled target.

entries.label: dot-dot-segments-raw-in-a-value
entries.why: Same class, unencoded on the wire, so url.QueryEscape is the only thing standing between it and the /auth query string.

entries.label: same-origin-absolute-url-percent-encoded
entries.why: tether#117 A3 class 2: an absolute URL on OUR origin passes an origin check while carrying an off-origin path.

entries.label: same-origin-absolute-url-raw
entries.why: Same class, unencoded: a raw '://' inside the query must not be able to restart the target as an absolute URL.

entries.label: backslash-and-protocol-relative-in-values
entries.why: The two shapes that navigated off-site against the pre-#225 guard: '\' is read as '/' for special schemes, and '//host' is protocol-relative.

entries.label: literal-tab-and-newline-inside-the-query
entries.why: WHATWG URL parsing strips tab/LF/CR before parsing, which is how '/<TAB>/evil.example' slipped past a startsWith check. No expectParams: the stripping is the point, so the values legitimately change.

entries.label: literal-hash-inside-the-raw-query
entries.why: Defensive: net/url splits the fragment off before RawQuery is set, so this cannot arrive over the wire today. It pins the producer against a future caller that assigns RawQuery from another source.
